item.title: Smart Glasses and AI Platform for Emergency Medical Services
item.description:
January 2021 – Present

Associated with Pace University

Designed and developed an AI-enabled smart glasses platform to support real-time communication, clinical documentation, and decision support for emergency medical services (EMS).

  • Developed hands-free smart glasses, AI-assisted documentation, and clinical decision support systems.
  • Evaluated the platform with 30+ EMS teams and 120+ EMS/ED providers through user-centered design and usability studies.
  • Published peer-reviewed research in CSCW, ICHI, IJHCI, and AMIA.

Smart Glasses Prototype

The wearable interface supports hands-free access to information while allowing EMS providers to remain focused on patient care and clinical tasks.

Demonstration and Research Exchange

The platform has been demonstrated to researchers and clinical collaborators to gather feedback on usability, workflow integration, and future deployment in prehospital care.

item.title: AI-Enabled Sports Performance & Athlete Development
item.description:

Associated with United Chinese Basketball Association

Designed and developed AI-driven technologies supporting athlete evaluation, basketball analytics, and community engagement.

  • Developed BERT- and deep learning-based models for player ranking using scouting reports, game statistics, and media evaluations.
  • Built computer vision pipelines for basketball action recognition and real-time performance analysis.
  • Designed a basketball community platform integrating player engagement, court discovery, and event management.

Player Development in Practice

Alongside analytics development, I observe and document high-level youth basketball training to connect technical models with real coaching environments. Sessions with the New York Rens AAU program—which featured Don Bosco Prep guard , the No. 2 overall player in the 2024 high school class—inform my understanding of player development, practice design, and the on-court context behind performance data.

item.title: 🥽 EMS Documentation Simulation Study
item.description:
I finally finished my last piece of dissertation work - AI-enabled documentation system featured AR-based smart glasses for EMS in both CO and NYC with my advisor, Dr. ! Thanks for the organization and simulation setup support from , MD, MPH/MSPH (as well as Nicolena Mitchell and Carl Elston), and , PhD, DNP, MS, MPH, RN, FSSH, FAAN. Four months after finishing at the Mount Sinai STAR Center, we had a great journey in Denver!

Ideation

This system was designed around a simple goal: capture patient care process as it happens without taking providers’ hands or attention away from the patient. The smart-glass application supports medication scanning, contextual photo and video capture, and flexible voice dictation during care. Captured information is then transferred to a connected tablet-based EHR interface for transcription and documentation support.

The AI transforms reviewed dictation into structured field suggestions and an editable patient-care narrative. Clinicians can inspect highlighted evidence, correct extracted values, change the destination EHR field, and choose whether to append, replace, or reject each suggestion. This human-in-the-loop design preserves clinician control while shifting EMS documentation from a delayed, recall-based task toward a real-time capture-and-review workflow.

- Hands-Free Capture

Beautiful Denver

Come, lend an ear to Denver’s song,
where dawn lays gold on Sinai’s crown,
and every winding mountain road
leads weary scholars out of town.

High on the ridge, where thin winds race,
bold riders fly down stone and pine;
below, North Table Mountain keeps
its silent watch like some old shrine.

Then thunder moved across the grass—
not storm, nor drum, nor marching men,
but bison beneath a bruised-blue sky,
with distant Denver beyond the fen.

At Boulder, halls of ruddy stone
stood warm beneath the western light;
while ancient rocks, rain-dark and red,
rose like old keeps against the night.

And when the road had claimed its due,
we found where lamps and barrels gleam;
a modest feast, a traveler’s cup,
and one last toast to field and dream.

item.title: 🏀 Asian Coach Clinic
item.description:
Asian Coach Clinic

brought a group of accomplished Asian basketball coaches to the United States for an exchange focused on coaching practice, player development, and high-performance training. The program began in Los Angeles, where the delegation attended NBA All-Star events at Intuit Dome, before continuing to the University of Missouri. At Mizzou, the group observed team practices and studied modern five-out offense, defensive principles, and strength and conditioning methods with the Tigers’ coaching and performance staff.

Guests included UCBA representatives Enze Bai and Chairman ; Chinese national-team strength and conditioning coach and basketball commentator ; former China U15 women’s national-team coach and CUBA Guangzhou College of Applied Science and Technology men’s basketball head coach ; Singapore national-team assistant coach and Indonesia National U18 Basketball Coach and SMA Jubilee Jakarta Head Coach . The clinic concluded with a group visit to the Gateway Arch in St. Louis—a fitting final stop for a week built around learning, connection, and the shared language of basketball.

Los Angeles · NBA All-Star at Intuit Dome

Columbia · Learning with Mizzou Basketball

Performance coach shared how training load, recovery data, periodization, nutrition, hydration, and sleep can inform daily decisions for high- and low-minute athletes.
